methodology_note: Benchmark-based. Efficiency estimates derived from model training data on Agentforce/Apex AI-assisted delivery patterns. Not a commitment. Applies to PS delivery effort — not Claro-side dependencies, UAT, or legal gates.

engagement_profile.fixed_timeline_note: Timeline is client-committed and non-negotiable. Efficiency manifests as quality uplift and schedule buffer — not calendar compression.

high.label: High AI Leverage
high.description: Epics where AI tooling (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, AI test generation) materially accelerates code authoring, boilerplate generation, and unit test coverage. Estimated 30–40% effort reduction on PS build time.
high.rationale: Apex Queueable chains, AST Walker algorithm, and DLQ/Finalizer patterns are highly repetitive, pattern-driven code. AI code generation eliminates boilerplate; AI test generation reaches ≥85% coverage faster. The cursor and byte-offset patterns in E01 are well-established in training data.

medium_high.label: Medium-High AI Leverage
medium_high.description: Epics where AI accelerates service scaffolding, Prompt Template authoring, and invocable wiring. Estimated 25–35% effort reduction.
medium_high.rationale: LLM compilation engine (E02) and diagnostic narrative (E05) both involve ConnectApi callout service classes and Prompt Template configuration. AI can scaffold the service layer and generate few-shot examples for the Prompt Templates faster than manual authoring.

medium.label: Medium AI Leverage
medium.description: Epics where AI helps with declarative configuration, instruction authoring, and CMDT data generation. Estimated 15–25% effort reduction.
medium.rationale: Agent subagent instructions and action wiring (E06/E07) benefit from AI-assisted natural-language instruction authoring and test scenario generation. CMDT seed data (E09) is tedious but AI can generate correctly-structured XML/JSON from a schema spec quickly.

low.label: Low AI Leverage
low.description: Epics or activities where the constraint is human decisions, Claro dependencies, or click-by-click platform configuration. AI tooling < 15% impact.
low.rationale: E08 LWC layout is driven by Claro SME iteration cycles — AI scaffolding helps but iteration speed is capped by the feedback loop with Lucas. E10 LGPD gate is a legal sign-off — ETL click-by-click configuration, documentation drafting benefits from AI but the gate itself is a human dependency. UAT and parallel run are Claro-analyst activities.

fixed_timeline_implications.note: Timeline is fixed at 8 weeks. Efficiency does NOT compress the schedule — it creates buffer and quality headroom within the same calendar.
benefits: Sprint 1: CPU ceiling spike and peer review absorb buffer — no S1 overrun risk
Sprint 2: Three epics (E02+E03+E04) complete within one week without overtime risk — confirmed by 30–40% compression on the two heaviest custom Apex epics
Sprint 3: Sprint 3 is the most loaded (4 epics + SIT→UAT deploy). AI leverage on E05 and E08 scaffolding creates room for agent precision iteration (E06/E07) within the same week
P2 UAT: Build sprint buffer means fewer open defects entering UAT — reduces UAT rework cycles
P0: CMDT seed and permset generation (E09) absorbed into P0 — TA freed for architecture decisions rather than configuration typing
fixed_timeline_implications.risk_reduction: The 3-sprint Build window (3 weeks) is the highest-risk phase for an SC engagement. AI-native delivery converts that risk from schedule risk to quality risk — the team ships more complete, better-tested work rather than rushing to meet sprint dates.

quality_uplifts: Unit test coverage reaches ≥85% per class with AI test generation — target met in Sprint 1, not Sprint 3
Prompt Template few-shot examples richer — more iteration cycles in Sprint 2 before UAT
Agent subagent instruction quality higher — AI drafts reviewed by TA rather than authored from scratch
RunSpecifiedTests registry more complete — AI generates from class list rather than manual enumeration
where_ai_does_not_help: GAP-001: Knowledge Articles — Claro content dependency, no AI shortcut
GAP-002: Agentforce license — Salesforce provisioning, no AI shortcut
GAP-003: Sandbox provisioning — Claro IT, no AI shortcut
GAP-004: RunSpecifiedTests registry — PS + Claro DevOps must agree manually
GAP-005: LGPD legal sign-off — human gate, Week 6 is fixed
GAP-006: CSV volumetry — requires real Claro data, not model prediction

benchmark_disclaimer: Efficiency estimates are benchmark-based, derived from model training data on Agentforce and Apex AI-assisted delivery patterns. Actual compression depends on team proficiency with AI tooling, Claro data availability, and sandbox stability. These figures are decision-support for internal PS planning — not a client commitment.
